data.name: evaluation_description
data.value:
Discover opportunities to optimise activity and workflow YAML grammar and syntax so that expressions can be written in shorthand. Today `when` is the only construct with a compound, language-like expression syntax; the structured `condition` tree is marked LEGACY in its favour yet remains the only available form on actions, reusable fragments and transitions, and technique bindings carry their own separate literal/rename/template deviation forms.

Authoritative current-state sources: the Zod schemas under `src/schema/` (notably `when-expression.ts` and `condition.schema.ts`), the JSON Schemas under `schemas/`, and the 140-file YAML definition corpus under `workflows/`. The `docs/` specifications are in scope as consumers of the grammar that may require updating, not as an authority on it. `grammar/activity.ebnf` and `constraints/activity.als` are placeholders for future work and carry no evidential weight for the current grammar.

The run settles a target grammar covering both activity and workflow definitions and specifies it precisely enough that four formal artifacts could be generated from that specification: `grammar/activity.ebnf` and `constraints/activity.als` brought into alignment, plus new counterparts `grammar/workflow.ebnf` and `constraints/workflow.als`. Those four files are the specification's target consumers, produced by follow-on implementation work; this run does not write them. All output of this run stays within the planning folder.
